messages:
incident-bot: [P1] geo-dns alert — elevated SERVFAIL rates observed by external resolvers (Cloudflare/ISP) for redwood-inference.com in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1. Impact: intermittent API failures, ~15% error rate for generation requests routed to those regions. Paging @oncall.
Anna: oncall here. seeing spike on our edge-proxy metrics too. retries spiking. starting impact triage. :eyes:
Mike: I'm checking Route53 health checks and Cloudflare resolver logs. initial hunch: asymmetric propagation after a recent failover we triggered earlier today. Not sure if it's our TTLs or upstream caching.
Lina: Client reports from EU show 502s and some DNS lookup timeouts when hitting the regional edge hostnames. Can we confirm which names are returning NX/T/T? I'll run dig from a few vantage points.
Raj: Dig outputs from two vantage points (eu-west probe and ap-south probe):

```
; eu-west probe
$ dig +short redwood-inference.com A @1.1.1.1
; returns empty (SERVFAIL)

; ap-south probe
$ dig +short redwood-inference.com A @8.8.8.8
; returns IPs but with inconsistent TTLs (varies between 30s and 300s)
```

So resolvers disagree.
Anna: Good, that matches the errors. What changed? Mike, you said we triggered a failover earlier — when and what exactly?
Mike: We performed a manual geo-failover at 14:03 UTC to move traffic away from eu-west AZ-B which had an AWS ENI flap. That updated a weighted Route53 record and pushed a Cloudflare backup origin. The Route53 change was a small TTL tweak (set to 60s) and then we reverted some weights after stabilization. I see some queued Route53 change batches around 14:10.
Sam: AWS change history shows some CREATE/DELETE on the geo A records. Cloudflare shows cached old answers at some edge PoPs. Looks like some resolvers cached a negative answer (SERVFAIL) during the change window and are not honoring the low TTL — maybe due to upstream resolver heuristics.
Cody: Customers behind certain corporate resolvers (we've seen this before) tend to aggressively cache SERVFAILs for several minutes. Could be causing the 15% persistent error.
Lina: Agree. Short-term mitigation idea: re-add a minimal fallback A record set with different low-ttl name (edge-fallback.redwood-inference.com) and update Route53 alias to include it so resolvers that re-query get a live IP. Downsides: more DNS churn.
Anna: We need to coordinate with Cloudflare support as well — if their authoritative cache is serving bad state, they can purge or force a revalidation. Mike, can you open a ticket and request evicting the TTL clobber in impacted PoPs? Include list of border ASN/probe IPs.
Mike: Opening ticket now. Ticket# CF-99233 (link: https://support.cloudflare.com/tickets/CF-99233). Asked them to target eu-west and ap-south edge caches and to check for cached SERVFAIL("served by us") entries. Also asked for guidance on whether the cached negative TTL was elevated for certain ISPs.
Raj: Meanwhile I'm going to temporarily raise our client-side retry/backoff and add a fast fallback to other regions for affected routes. Pushing a quick patch to edge-proxy config: increase retries to 4 and exponential backoff with jitter. Will monitor 5xx rate.
Anna: Good. Also notify SREs to pause any additional DNS changes. We don't want overlapping churn.
Sam: Observability note: adding an eval to track resolver error codes per client ASN to map impacted customers. Saving logs to incident workspace.
Cody: I've drafted a status note for customers: short blurb explaining partial outage to EU/AP customers due to external DNS propagation/resolver behavior. Will wait for CF confirmation before posting.
Lina: Cloudflare replied: they see high cache miss + some SERVFAILs at certain PoPs; they've performed a targeted cache purge for our zone and are forcing revalidation. They suggest we keep TTL at 60s for 10 mins to allow repropagation then gradually increase. CF also flagged a handful of ISP resolvers returning stale negative caching.
Anna: Action list so far: 1) Mike: keep CF ticket open and confirm purge complete. 2) Raj: rollback edge-proxy retry change if it causes overload; monitor. 3) Sam: map impacted ASNs and notify account teams for big customers. 4) Cody: hold customer note until CF confirms purge. 5) Lina: monitor dig across probes every 30s. Anyone disagree?
Mike: Locking DNS changes. CF confirmed purge complete at 14:38 UTC and they performed revalidation. I see dig responses returning healthy IPs from most probes.
Raj: Error rate dropped from 15% -> 2% in the last 10 minutes after CF purge + our retries. Some corporate ASNs still show 5-8% error — probably due to long negative cache in their resolvers.
Sam: Mapping shows five ASNs with persistent SERVFAIL behavior. Reached out to account owners for direct customer notifications.
Cody: Posting incident banner in app now with status: Partial DNS issues in EU/AP affecting some customers; mitigation in progress. Link to status page: https://status.redwood.com/incident/2812345678
Anna: OK team — continue monitoring for 1 hour, then reconvene for postmortem if stable. Collect timeline, TTLs, and CSPROBE outputs. Tentative sev1->sev3 after impact drops below 1% for 30 minutes.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigating, impacted_regions=[eu-west-1, ap-south-1], assignees=[Anna, Mike, Raj], incident_id=INC-2026-2812345678.
